verdict.rationale: Clerk documents OAuth client registration for MCP clients through both Client ID Metadata Documents and Dynamic Client Registration, which are the spec-relevant registration mechanisms. It also documents OAuth scoped access, custom OAuth scopes for MCP clients, and gating tool calls against the caller's scopes, so the core authorization-server role in front of an MCP server is evidenced. The evidence does not show an end-to-end guide for protecting your own MCP server or how resource servers verify the issued tokens. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of protecting a developer's own MCP server end-to-end, documented token verification and validation (e.g., JWT/introspection and audience checks) on the MCP server side, explicit MCP authorization-spec compliance claims (e.g., protected resource metadata), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can put a spec-compliant OAuth authorization flow in front of my MCP server so remote agents connect with scoped, verifiable tokens
